prompt: Explore the month-end trap: plusMonths clamps Jan 31 to Feb 29, so write addMonthsStickyEnd that instead keeps an end-of-month date on the end of the target month.
explanation: LocalDate.plusMonths never invents a day that does not exist, so it clamps: January 31 plus one month is the 29th (or 28th) of February. That clamping is lossy -- the information that the date meant "the end of the month" is gone, which is why adding a month again gives March 29 instead of March 31. Checking isLastDayOfMonth on the ORIGINAL date before shifting, then snapping the result with withDayOfMonth(lengthOfMonth()), preserves the intent that subscription and billing dates usually have.
hints: date.getDayOfMonth() == date.lengthOfMonth() is the whole of isLastDayOfMonth -- lengthOfMonth already knows about leap years.
In addMonthsStickyEnd, ask the question about the INPUT date, before plusMonths has clamped anything.
shifted.withDayOfMonth(shifted.lengthOfMonth()) moves a date onto the last day of whatever month it landed in.
